title: NSGo game import settings (version 1)
description: File is one asset's import settings and credit. It holds at least one section: at most one of Image, Audio, Font and Model, for how game assets imports the asset, and Credit for who made it and under what license.

version.description: Version is the schema version; it must equal CurrentVersion (1).

image.description: Image holds the settings of an image (PNG or JPEG).

audio.description: Audio holds the settings of a sound (WAV).

font.description: Font holds the settings of a font (TrueType or OpenType) that a font target bakes into a bitmap font.

model.description: Model holds the settings of a model (glTF or GLB) that a model target packs into one GLB file.

credit.description: Credit records who made the asset and its license, which game release and game credits list in the credits file; any kind of asset may carry one.

Audio.description: Audio holds how a sound is converted by an audio target. Each field left out keeps the target's setting in game.yaml.

format.description: Format is the output format: "wav", "aac" or "mp3".

rate.description: Rate is the output sample rate in Hz.

channels.description: Channels is 1 for mono or 2 for stereo.

peakDB.description: PeakDB normalizes the peak to this level in dBFS; it may not be set with RMSDB. Setting either replaces the target's normalization.

rmsDB.description: RMSDB normalizes the loudness to this level in dBFS with soft clipping; it may not be set with PeakDB.

bitrate.description: Bitrate is the AAC or MP3 bitrate in kbps.

loop.description: Loop is the region a player repeats, written into a WAV output's smpl chunk; AAC and MP3 carry no loop points, so a sound with a loop must be converted to WAV.

CellCollision.description: CellCollision overrides collision settings for one 0-based cell of a sliced sprite sheet.

cell.description: Cell is the 0-based cell index (row by row from the top left), matching the frame suffix _<cell>.

mode.description: Mode selects how collision shapes are generated for this cell: "alpha", "box", "ellipse", "polygon", or "none".

tolerance.description: Tolerance is the alpha cutoff in [0, 255] for "alpha", "box", and "ellipse" modes.

maxVertices.description: MaxVertices limits how many vertices each baked convex polygon may have (3 to 8; 0 uses 8).

points.description: Points lists explicit polygon vertices in untrimmed frame pixels when Mode is "polygon".

CellPivot.description: CellPivot overrides the normalized pivot for one 0-based cell of a sliced sprite sheet.

cell.description: Cell is the 0-based cell index (row by row from the top left), matching the frame suffix _<cell>.

pivot.description: Pivot is the normalized [x, y] pivot for this cell.

CellPoints.description: CellPoints overrides or adds named image points for one 0-based cell of a sliced sprite sheet.

cell.description: Cell is the 0-based cell index (row by row from the top left), matching the frame suffix _<cell>.

points.description: Points maps point names (such as "muzzle" or "feet") to [x, y] pixel coordinates in the untrimmed cell, overriding any default point of the same name.

Collision.description: Collision configures 2D collision shapes baked into packed atlas metadata when an atlas packs the image, as a default for every frame and optional per-cell overrides for a sliced sheet.

mode.description: Mode selects how collision shapes are generated: "alpha" (traced from pixel alpha), "box", "ellipse", "polygon" (using Points), or "none".

tolerance.description: Tolerance is the alpha cutoff in [0, 255] for "alpha", "box", and "ellipse" modes: pixels with alpha > Tolerance are treated as solid (0 treats any non-transparent pixel as solid).

maxVertices.description: MaxVertices limits how many vertices each baked convex polygon may have (3 to 8; 0 uses 8).

points.description: Points lists explicit polygon vertices in untrimmed frame pixels when Mode is "polygon" (at least 3 points; concave outlines are split into convex parts).

cells.description: Cells overrides collision settings for individual 0-based cells of a sliced sprite sheet, in ascending cell index order.

Credit.description: Credit records where an asset comes from, for the credits file a release ships with.

author.description: Author is who made the asset, a person, a group or a company, as its license asks it to be attributed.

license.description: License is the asset's license as an SPDX license expression, such as "CC0-1.0", "CC-BY-4.0" or "MIT OR Apache-2.0"; a license with no SPDX identifier is named "LicenseRef-" followed by a name of its own, with its terms in Notice.

source.description: Source is where the asset was obtained, usually a URL; empty for an asset made for the game.

notice.description: Notice is text the license requires to be shipped with the asset, such as a copyright line or a license's terms; it may span several lines.

Font.description: Font holds how a font target bakes a TrueType or OpenType font into an AngelCode BMFont. Each field left out keeps the target's setting in game.yaml.

size.description: Size is the font size in pixels the glyphs are drawn at; 0 keeps the target's.

chars.description: Chars are the characters baked into the font, each once, in any order, such as " 0123456789"; empty keeps the target's.

padding.description: Padding is the transparent gap around each glyph on the font's pages, in pixels.

Image.description: Image holds how an image is imported. A texture target reads Filter, Format, Mipmaps and SRGB; an atlas target reads Slice, Pivot, Collision, Points and CellPoints. Each field left out keeps the target's setting in game.yaml.

filter.description: Filter is the sampling filter written into the texture's KTX2 key/value data under FilterKey, which render3d.LoadKTX2 sets the sampler's filters from: "linear" or "nearest".

format.description: Format is the KTX2 compression format: "rgba8", "bc1", "bc3" or "etc2".

mipmaps.description: Mipmaps writes the whole mipmap chain down to 1x1 when true and only the full-size image when false.

srgb.description: SRGB marks the texture sRGB and filters its mipmaps in linear light when true.

slice.description: Slice cuts a sprite sheet into frames on a grid before an atlas packs them; nil packs the image as one frame.

pivot.description: Pivot sets the normalized pivot point(s) written to TexturePacker JSON when an atlas packs the image, as a default for every frame and optional per-cell overrides for a sliced sheet.

collision.description: Collision configures per-frame 2D collision shapes baked into packed atlas metadata when an atlas packs the image, as a default for every frame and optional per-cell overrides for a sliced sheet.

points.description: Points maps named image points (such as "muzzle" or "feet") to [x, y] pixel coordinates in the untrimmed frame, applied to an unsliced image and as defaults for every cell of a sliced sheet.

cellPoints.description: CellPoints overrides or adds named image points for individual 0-based cells of a sliced sprite sheet, in ascending cell index order.

Loop.description: Loop is a region of a sound in sample frames of the source file, from Start up to, but not including, End. A target that resamples the sound scales it to the new rate.

start.description: Start is the first frame of the loop.

end.description: End is the frame after the loop's last one; 0 is the end of the sound.

Model.description: Model holds how a model target packs a glTF model into one GLB file and how scenemodel builds its levels of detail. Each field left out keeps the target's setting in game.yaml.

scale.description: Scale multiplies the size of every scene of the model, such as 0.01 for a model exported in centimeters; 0 keeps the target's.

animations.description: Animations keeps the model's animations when true and leaves them out of the GLB when false.

lods.description: LODs declares the model's levels of detail from finest (index 0) to coarsest, with screen-ratio (and optional distance) thresholds. When omitted, scenemodel.Build pairs glTF nodes following the _LOD1, _LOD2 naming convention with default screen-ratio thresholds.

lodHysteresis.description: LODHysteresis is the optional relative deadband in [0, 0.5] used by render3d.Queue to prevent LOD popping near thresholds.

ModelLOD.description: ModelLOD describes one level of detail of a glTF model (Model.LODs), ordered from finest (LOD 0) to coarsest.

model.description: Model optionally names a separate glTF or GLB model file (slash-separated path from the project root) providing this level's geometry; empty uses this model file.

node.description: Node optionally names a node inside the model (this file, or Model when set) providing this level's geometry; cannot be combined with Mesh.

mesh.description: Mesh optionally names a mesh inside the model (this file, or Model when set) providing this level's geometry; cannot be combined with Node.

minScreenRatio.description: MinScreenRatio is the minimum projected viewport-height fraction in [0, 1] at which this level is drawn (render3d.LODLevel.MinScreenRatio). Levels must strictly decrease in MinScreenRatio; 0 marks an unbounded coarsest fallback.

maxDistance.description: MaxDistance is an optional maximum camera distance in world units at which this level is drawn (render3d.LODLevel.MaxDistance); 0 disables distance-based switching for this level.

Pivot.description: Pivot sets the normalized pivot points written into a packed atlas's TexturePacker frame metadata. Default applies to an unsliced image and to every cell of a sliced sheet without an entry in Cells.

default.description: Default is the normalized [x, y] pivot applied to an unsliced image and to every cell of a sliced sheet not listed in Cells.

cells.description: Cells overrides the normalized [x, y] pivot for individual 0-based cells of a sliced sprite sheet, in ascending cell index order.

Slice.description: Slice is the grid a sprite sheet is cut into, in pixels. Its cells are taken row by row from the top left, and frame i of the image name.png is packed as name_i.png.

width.description: Width and Height are each cell's size; both must be positive.

height.description: Width and Height are each cell's size; both must be positive.

margin.description: Margin is the gap between the image's top and left edges and the first row and column of cells.

spacing.description: Spacing is the gap between neighboring cells.

count.description: Count is how many cells are frames, counted from the first; 0 takes every cell that fits.
